sentences.text: 1  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal has been filed by the appellant State under Section 377 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for enhancement of sentence against the judgement and order NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004

JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined passed by the learned Joint District Judge & Additional Sessions Judge, (Fast Track Court), Sabarkantha @ Modasa (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Trial Court") in Sessions Case No. 205 of 2003 on 20.02.2004, whereby, the learned Trial Court was pleased to convict the respondents and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs. 100/- and in default, simple imprisonment of 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs. 100/- and in default, simple imprisonment of 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the IPC.

sentences.text: The learned Trial Court was pleased to order that the sentences of all the accused to run concurrently.

The learned Trial Court was further pleased to grant the accused the benefit of probation under Section 360 of Code of Criminal Procedure and released all the accused on probation of good conduct and directed that they be released on bond of Rs. 5000/- each with sureties of the like amount for a period of two years from the date of order.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined
The respondents are hereinafter referred to as the accused as they stood in the rank and file in the original case for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity.

2. The brief facts that emerge from the record of the case are as under:
2.1
That the accused no. 1 is the mother-in-law, accused no. 2 is the father-in-law and accused no. 3 is the husband of deceased Vinaben.

That Vinaben was married with accused no. 3 and all the accused demanded a buffalo from Vinaben and told her to bring the buffalo from her father or to bring money and also to bring money for the devotion to goddess Dashama and mentally and physically harassed the deceased Vinaben and abetted her to commit suicide.
That on 17.08.2003, deceased Vinaben sprinkled kerosene on herself and committed suicide.

That the complaint was filed by the complainant - Malabhai Nathabhai Malivad - father of the deceased Vinaben under Sections 498A, 306 and 114 of IPC and the same was registered at Malpur Police Station at I - C.R. No. 49/2003.

2.2 The Investigating Officer drew the necessary NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined panchnamas and recorded the statements of the connected witnesses and sent the body of deceased Vinaben for postmortem to the Community Health Centre, Malpur and after the necessary documents were collected, a charge- sheet came to be filed against the accused before the Sessions Court, Sabarkantha which was registered as Sessions Case No. 205/2003.

2.4 The prosecution has produced the following oral evidences in support of their case.

Sr. No. PW Particulars Exh.

After the learned APP filed the closing pursis at Exh. 27, the further statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded and after the arguments of the learned APP and the learned advocate for the accused were heard, the learned Trial Court by a judgement and order dated 20.02.2004 was pleased to convict the accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs. 100/- and in default, simple imprisonment of 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, rigorous NEUTRAL CITATION State Of Gujarat vs Dariyaben Prabhatbhai on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175788171/

sentences.text: 3 R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs. 100/- and in default, simple imprisonment of 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the IPC.
The learned Trial Court was pleased to order that the sentences of all the accused to run concurrently.

The learned Trial Court was further pleased to grant the benefit of probation under Section 360 of Code of Criminal Procedure on furnishing a bond of Rs. 5000/- each and to keep good behaviour and also not to involve themselves in any criminal activities during the probation period of two years from the date of order.

3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgement and order of conviction and granting benefit of probation to the accused, the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the order of sentence in respect of the offence under Section 306 of IPC is unduly lenient and grossly inadequate.

That the learned Trial Court ought to have inflicted the maximum sentence provided under Section 306 of IPC and all the accused should have been punished for imprisonment for a term extending to ten NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/06/2024 undefined years and fine.

That the sentence of rigorous imprisonment for three years is grossly inadequate and the learned Trial Court has not given any special reasons for inflicting a sentence which is less then what is provided under the Act.
The learned Trial Court ought to have imposed a deterrent sentence in such cases and the judgement and order of sentence is grossly inadequate and deserves to be enhanced.

4. Heard learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri for the appellant - State and learned advocate Ms. N.K.
Anandjiwala for the respondent.
Perused the impugned judgement and order of acquittal and have appreciated the entire evidence of the prosecution on record of the case.

5. Learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri has taken this Court through the entire evidence produced by the prosecution and has submitted that the learned Trial Court has failed to appreciate that a young married woman has committed suicide in a gross manner and has lost her life and she has in her own house sprinkled kerosene on herself and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined committed suicide. That the prosecution has brought the evidence of the father, mother and uncles and aunt of the deceased who all have deposed that the accused used to harass deceased Vinaben and they used to demand for a buffalo and money from her and they did not gave her any money for the devotion to goddess Dashama and she had to taken money from her parental house for the same.

That even though the prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubts and the accused have been found guilty, the learned Trial Court without assigning any proper reasons has given the benefit of probation to all the accused.

That the postmortem note and the evidence of the Medical Officer who had conducted the postmortem shows that deceased Vinaben had suffered 100% second degree burns and all the burn injuries were antemortem in nature.

That the learned Trial Court has been very lenient and has only sentenced the accused for a period of three years which is inadequate and also the benefit of probation has been granted but the same must be set aside and the accused be taken in custody and the sentence of three years must be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/06/2024 undefined enhanced to a maximum of ten years.
Learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri has urged this Court to allow the appeal and to take the accused in custody for suffering the sentence.

sentences.text: 4 6. Learned advocate Ms. N.K. Anandjiwala for the respondents has submitted that the judgement and order of conviction was passed by the learned Sessions Court on 20.02.2004 and as per the judgement and order, the respondents have been released on probation for a period of two years.
That the said probation period of two years had expired on 20.02.2006 and the appeal of the appellant - State has been admitted by an order of this Court on 06.07.2007.
That the appeal has been admitted after the period of probation is completed and the respondents have already suffered the sentence and hence, no interference is required.

Moreover, if the entire evidence is perused,
there is no evidence to convict the respondents as there is no evidence on record that at the time of the offence, the accused were at home.

Moreover, there is no evidence that the respondents had ill-treated the deceased Vinaben or that they were demanding buffalo or cash from her as the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined only evidence that has come on record is from the parental side of deceased Vinaben who have only stated things that they had heard.

That no independent witnesses have been examined by the prosecution and there is no evidence of any neighbours or any independent persons to show that in fact, deceased Vinaben was mentally and physically harassed by the respondents.

That the respondents have filed the bail bonds as per the order of the learned Trial Court and the period of probation of two years had elapsed long back and there is a huge delay of 20 years and it would not be in the interest of justice to set aside the impugned order and enhance the sentence of the respondents.
That the prosecution has not made out a case for enhancement and hence, the appeal must be rejected.

7. The short question to be decided by this Court is as to whether the sentence imposed by the learned Trial Court in the impugned judgement and order is sufficient or not? and as to whether the grant of probation to the respondents by the learned Trial Court was just and proper?.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined 8.
To come to e just conclusion it would be in the fitness of things to reappreciate the entire evidence produced by the prosecution on record and to bring home the charge against the accused

, the prosecution has examined PW1 - Shanaji Khatuji at Exh. 12 and Shanaji Viraji at Exh. 14 and both the witnesses are the panch witnesses of the panchnama of the place of offence and they have stated that on 18.08.2003, they were called to Malpur Police Station.

The witnesses have identified their signatures on the documents produced at Exh. 13 which is the panchnama of the place of offence and the witnesses have stated that the place of offence was shown by Balwantbhai Nathabhai.
During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused
, the witness has stated that they had not gone to the place of offence and they had affixed their signatures at the Police Station.

On appreciation of the evidences, both these witnesses who are the panch witnesses of the place of offence, both the witnesses have not been declared hostile by the learned Trial Court but it appears that the witnesses have stated NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/06/2024 undefined that they have not gone to the place of offence and have merely affixed their signatures on the panchnama in the Police Station and hence, the panchnama of the place of offence is not proved from the depositions of the panch witnesses.

sentences.text: The prosecution has examined PW3 - Dr. Pankajbhai Gopalram Soni at Exh. 15 and the witness is the Medical Officer who had conducted the postmortem on the dead body of deceased Vinaben Kiranbhai Pagi on 18.08.2003 at Community Health Centre, Malpur.

The witness has fully supported the case of prosecution and has stated that he and panel Dr. Vipul Prajapti had conducted the postmortem and had prepared the postmortem note which is produced at Exh. 16.

As per the deposition of the witness and the postmortem note produced at Exh. 16, the burn injuries on the dead body of deceased Vinaben Kiranbhai Pagi were antemortem and as per column no. 17, the following injuries were found:
 1) Hairs partially burn.
2) Superficial skin of face burnt with bleeding from the nose and mouth and eyes.
Tongue protruded with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined air bubbling.

3) Superficial skin burnt of front and back of chest with reddish demarcation.
4) Superficial skin burnt of front and back of abdomen and upper limbs (both) with cyonosed palms.
5) Superficial skin burnt of front and back of lower limbs (except sole) and genitals.
During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the witness has stated that postmortem was conducted on the basis of the yadi which is produced at Exh. 17 and the body was identified by Police Sub- Inspector, Malpur Police Station.
That the dead body had clothes which were not burnt and burns were found from the top of the head till the legs of dead body and kerosene smell was found on the dead body.
8.2 The prosecution has examined PW4 - Malabhai Nathabhai at Exh. 18 and this witness is the complainant and father of the deceased Vinaben.

The witness has stated that Vinaben was married to the accused no. 3 about four years ago and she used to reside in her matrimonial home with the respondents and had come to visit them ten days NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined before the devotion to goddess Dashama.
That at that time she had told them that her father-in-law and mother-in-law were demanding for a buffalo or for money and had threatened to kill her.

That his daughter wanted to do the devotion to goddess Dashama and told him that her father- in-law and mother-in-law were not giving her money for the same and hence, he had given her Rs. 500/- and made her sit in a jeep and sent her back to her matrimonial home.
That on 17.08.2002, his nephew - Bhemabhai Pujabhai Khant telephoned him and told him that his daughter Vinaben is burnt and he, his son and other relatives went to Lalpur.
That he met his nephew who told them that Vinaben had expired and he told everyone in the village and many persons came in a tempo and a jeep came to Lalpur.
That they went to Vinaben's house but the house was closed and the elders of the community wanted to see the dead body and they went to the Police Station.
That the police came and opened the house and saw Vinaben in a burned condition and bleeding from the mouth.

That he had filed the complaint which is produced at Exh.
18.

During the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the witness has stated that his State Of Gujarat vs Dariyaben Prabhatbhai on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175788171/
6 nephew - Bhemabhai Pujabhai Khant had informed him that Vinaben had expired and the news was given on the telephone on 17.08.2003.

sentences.text: That from his village to go to Lalpur, Malpur Police Station is on the way at Ambaliya village and they had gone to Malpur Police Station to inform the police.

That his nephew - Bhemabhai Pujabhai Khant had telephoned him and informed him that Vinaben was burnt while she was making rotlas but he did not take his nephew - Bhemabhai Pujabhai Khant to the Police Station.
That the police had come and opened the house.
That he was married twice and earlier he was married to a girl from Jograna village and she was found dead in a well.
That he had a doubt that his daughter was murdered and he had given a complaint of murder in Malpur Police Station.

That the complaint which is produced at Exh. 19 was not recorded as per his say and he had stated that his daughter was murdered and he had shown a blood stained axe and a stick to the police which was seized by the police in his presence.

That at the place of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined incident, no soot was found and as per his complaint, his daughter was murdered but the same was not taken down as per his say.
8.3 The prosecution has examined PW5 - Virabhai Nathabhai Malivad at Exh. 21, PW6 - Somabhai Nathabhai Malivad at Exh. 22 and PW7 - Maniben Virabhai at Exh. 23.
The witnesses are the uncles and aunt respectively of deceased Vinaben and they have supported the case of prosecution and have stated that they had gone to Malpur when they heard the news.

During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, all the witnesses have stated in their statements before the police that Vinaben was murdered and they had a doubt that she was murdered but the police have not recorded the statements or complaint as per their say.
They had a doubt that Vinaben was murdered and the nephew had told them that Vinaben had sustained burn injuries while she was making rotlas.
That when they went to Lalpur, they saw the dead body of Vinaben which was near the stove.
8.4 The prosecution has examined PW8 - Maniben NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined Malabhai Malivad at Exh. 24 and the witness is the mother of deceased Vinaben.

The witness has stated that the deceased was married to Kiranbhai Prabhatbhai before four years and whenever she would come, she would tell her that the accused are demanding for a buffalo or money and they were mentally and physically harassing her.
That they used to send her back to the matrimonial house as they did not wish to break her house and she had asked for money to do the devotion to goddess Dashama and she had given her Rs. 500/-.
That her nephew had phoned and told her that Vinaben had sustained burn injuries while making rotlas and they had gone to Lalpur and saw the dead body of Vinaben.
That the complaint was filed by her husband in the Malpur Police Station and the accused have killed her daughter Vinaben

. During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the witness has stated that the police had not recorded her statement and her nephew - Bhemaji had informed them on the phone that Vinaben sustained injuries while making rotlas and hence, they had all gone to the village.

That Vinaben was lying near NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/06/2024 undefined the stove and there were no clothes on her body and the hairs on her head were burnt and a skirt was thrown on her body.

That her daughter had sustained burn injuries while she was making rotlas and they had a doubt that the accused have committed the murder of her State Of Gujarat vs Dariyaben Prabhatbhai on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175788171/
7 daughter.

sentences.text: 8.5 The prosecution has examined PW9 - Sawabhai Kalubhai Malivad at Exh. 25 and this witness is a relative of deceased Vinaben.

The witness has supported the case of prosecution and he has stated that after they heard the news, they had gone to the matrimonial home of Vinaben but no one was at home and they went to the Police Station and brought the police and they saw the dead body.
That kerosene smell was found on the dead body and the body was burnt but the hairs on the head were not burnt.
That they had asked Malabhai why Vinaben had done so and Malabhai had told him that Vinaben used to say that the accused had demanded for a buffalo.

During the cross- examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the witness has stated that he has stated about the cruelty to Vinaben as per the say of Vinaben's father and he has no NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined personal knowledge of the same.
That the police has not recorded his statement and the police had written his statement of their own accord.

8.6 The prosecution has examined PW10 - Kalubhai Harjibhai Desai at Exh. 26 and the witness is the Police Sub-Inspector, Malpur Police Station and the Investigating Officer and he has stated that the complaint was filed by the complainant in his presence and he had prepared the inquest panchnama and the panchnama of the place of offence and had thereafter, recorded the statements of the connected witnesses.
That he had arrested the accused and had thereafter, filed the charge-sheet before the learned Trial Court.
During the cross-examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the witness has stated that there were no soot marks found in the kitchen on the ceiling and nothing was burnt in the house.

That the place where the dead body was found burnt,
had no marks of burns and there were burned clothes on the body of the deceased.

That the deceased had never filed any complaint about any harassment by the accused and during investigation, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined statement of Bhemaji Punaji was not recorded.

That he has not recorded the statements of any witnesses of Lalpur village and during investigation, he had not found any evidence that the accused were demanding for buffalo from the deceased prior to her death.
That he had not found any evidence from the village of the accused that the deceased was ill-treated by the accused.
That during investigation, there was no evidence that the accused had taken an axe and a stick and killed the deceased.

9. On appreciating the entire evidence of the witness, the prosecution has produced the evidence of the father, mother, uncles, aunts and the relatives of deceased Vinaben but they all were not residents of village Lalpur which was the matrimonial house of the deceased Vinaben.

That there is no independent witness who has supported the case of prosecution to show that the accused were mentally and physically harassing the deceased and there is evidence that the nephew - Bhemaji Punaji Khant had informed the complainant that Vinaben had sustained injuries while she was making rotlas but the said nephew - Bhemaji Punaji NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined Khant has not been examined before the learned Trial Court.

As per the case of prosecution, Bhemaji Punaji Khant was the first person to know about the incident of Vinaben and the whereabouts of the accused prior to the incident, at the time of the incident or thereafter has not come on record.

That from the evidence of Bhemaji Punaji Khant, the evidence about how the incident occurred, the time of the incident or whether Bhemaji Punaji Khant was an eye witness would have come on record and as the said important witness Bhemaji Punaji State Of Gujarat vs Dariyaben Prabhatbhai on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175788171/
8

Khant has not been examined before the learned Trial Court, important aspects have not come on record and it has also not come on record as to how the information about deceased Vinaben being burnt was known to the nephew.

Moreover, in the evidence of the Investigating Officer, it has come on record that the place where deceased Vinaben was lying, did not bear any burn marks and the ceiling did not have any marks of soot around.

It appears that no examination of the place of offence by the FSL was undertaken and even in the panchnama of the place of offence which is produced at NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined Exh. 13, no burn marks are found but an empty plastic gallon was found which smelled of kerosene.
That in the house vessels, two cots with quilts and wood with grass on it was found.

10. Having minutely dissected the evidence produced by the prosecution on record, the incident has occurred way back on 17.08.2003 and the impugned judgement and order of sentence was passed on 20.02.2004.

The learned Trial Court deemed it proper to release all the accused on probation on bond of Rs. 5000/- with sureties of like amount and on condition that they would keep good behaviour and not involve in any criminal activities and not leave the State of Gujarat for a period of two years.

That after the accused were released on probation, the prosecution has not produced any evidence to show that the accused have been involved in any criminal activities and antecedents of the accused have remained unblemished.
After a huge gap of almost 20 years, this Court does not deem it fit to send the accused to jail as the same would not subserve the ends of justice.

The Appellate Court has NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined jurisdiction to enhance the sentence but the jurisdiction is required to be exercised sparingly and it has also to be seen whether the discretion exercised by the learned Trial Court of releasing the accused on probation of good conduct has been properly exercised or not and whether it is in fitness of things to award any sentence of imprisonment to the accused after a huge gap of 20 years after the occurrence of the offence.

Considering the evidence produced by the prosecution on record as discussed above, this Court does not find any reason to interfere with the impugned judgement and order of the learned Trial Court and it is settled law
that even where the discretion of granting probation was improperly exercised by the learned Trial Court, the High Court should not interfere
after the period of probation had expired
. That the period of probation has expired almost 18 years ago and on this ground also the order with regard to release the accused on probation of good conduct cannot be interfered with.

Moreover, considering the evidence of the prosecution, the accused have a good case on merits and hence, the question is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1271/2004 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined answered accordingly.
11.
For the reasons stated above, the appeal of the appellant fails and is hereby dismissed.

The impugned judgement and order passed by the learned Joint District Judge & Additional Sessions Judge, (Fast Track Court), Sabarkantha at Modasa in Sessions Case No. 205 of 2003 on 20.02.2004 is hereby confirmed.
12. Bail bonds stand cancelled.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Trial Court forthwith.
(S. V. PINTO,J)
